title: Etale comparison reflects universal coefficient normalization
statement: Let Z be a scheme, R and S finite commutative rings in Type(u+1), and q:R→S. Let C and Cprime be bounded derived fixed-ring module sheaves on Z_et and δ:C→Res_q(Cprime). Apply exact etale-to-proetale comparison to δ and follow by the canonical localIsomorphismComparisonCoefficients(q) at Cprime [def-weil-pbc-derived-local-isomorphism-sheaf, def-weil-pbc-derived-normalization-arrows]. If that specified arrow is initial in the structured-arrow category for proetale derived scalar restriction, then δ is initial in the structured-arrow category for etale derived scalar restriction. There is no adic tower, actual pulled coefficient presentation, marking, or further etale source in this assertion.

source.place: Tags 06YS (K-flat resolutions), 0G7E (pullback preserves K-flat complexes with flat terms), and 0D6D (composition of derived pullbacks). Also proetale.tex Tag 09B1 for exact conservative comparison, or the small etale site Tag 03ED for etale source restriction, respectively.

proof.text: Use K-flat resolutions with flat terms for extension of coefficients in the fixed-ring sheaf category, identified with modules over the constant ring sheaf. Comparison inverse image preserves such resolutions. The two orders of inverse image and scalar extension give the same sheafified tensor complex, with the unit x↦1 tensor x. Hence the inverse scalar mate of the specified restriction square is invertible.

Initiality of the compared arrow says that its scalar adjunct is invertible. By the mate unit identity this adjunct is comparison applied to the etale scalar adjunct, conjugated by the preceding tensor comparison. Comparison inverse image is exact and conservative on sheaves, since its sheaf unit is invertible; applying homology to a cone therefore shows that it reflects derived isomorphisms. Thus the etale adjunct is invertible. Transporting the initial scalar-adjunction unit along it proves the conclusion. This does not require a Tor bound; zero rings, zero complexes and empty schemes are included.

theorem comparisonNormalization_reflects_universal (Z : Scheme.{u})
    {R S : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Finite R] [Finite S]
    (q : R →+* S)
    {C : DerivedCategory (Sheaf Z.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} R))}
    {C' : DerivedCategory (Sheaf Z.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} S))}
    (_hC : ∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, i < a ∨ b < i →
      IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ i).obj C))
    (_hC' : ∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, i < a ∨ b < i →
      IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ i).obj C'))
    (δ : C ⟶ (normalizationRestrict Z.smallEtaleTopology q).obj C')
    (h : Nonempty (StructuredArrow.IsUniversal
      (StructuredArrow.mk
        ((ProEtale.comparisonUpperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} R) Z).mapDerivedCategory.map δ ≫
          (localIsomorphismComparisonCoefficients q).hom.app C') :
        StructuredArrow _ (normalizationRestrict (ProEt.topology Z) q)))) :
    Nonempty (StructuredArrow.IsUniversal
      (StructuredArrow.mk δ : StructuredArrow _
        (normalizationRestrict Z.smallEtaleTopology q)))
